original_question: Let G be a connected semisimple algebraic group, let V be a finite-dimensional algebraic G-module whose stabilizer in G of a point in general position is trivial, and let σ be an automorphism of G. If σV denotes the same underlying variety V equipped with the twisted G-action g·v := σ(g)·v, can there exist such data for which V and σV are not birationally G-isomorphic as G-varieties?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 3, introduced as the generalization of Problem 2 after defining the twisted action σX.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the semisimple connected group G, the finite-dimensional algebraic G-module V, the trivial stabilizer condition in general position, the twisting by an automorphism σ, and the birational G-nonequivalence question for V versus σV. This is exactly the linear-module problem Popov formulates in Section 1 as Problem 3, rather than the broader variant for arbitrary G-varieties.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed base field k of characteristic 0; this global assumption should be stated to make the question fully stand-alone.
V should be understood as a finite-dimensional algebraic G-module over k, i.e. a linear G-variety.
It helps to spell out that 'birationally G-isomorphic' means that there exists a G-equivariant birational map from V to σV.

The nearby discussion notes that only outer automorphisms are genuinely relevant, since twisting by an inner automorphism gives an isomorphic G-variety; this is contextual rather than part of the official problem statement, but it is part of the paper-faithful scope.
The paper also warns not to broaden the question from linear G-modules to arbitrary G-varieties X, because in that broader setting the answer is already known to be positive.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Does there exist a connected semisimple algebraic k-group G, a finite-dimensional algebraic G-module V whose stabilizers of points in general position are trivial, and an automorphism σ of G, such that, if σV denotes the same underlying variety V endowed with the twisted G-action g·v := σ(g)·v, then there is no G-equivariant birational map from V to σV; equivalently, V and σV are not birationally G-isomorphic as G-varieties?
justification: The draft is essentially a restatement of the paper's Section 1, Problem 3. Popov first recalls Katsylo's conjecture on birational classification of generically free linear representations, then asks in Problem 2 about V versus V*, and immediately generalizes that to Problem 3 by defining the twisted action σX and asking whether V and σV can fail to be birationally G-isomorphic. The only substantive omissions from your draft are the paper's ambient field hypothesis and the explicit formulation of birational G-isomorphism as existence of a G-equivariant birational map. The surrounding remarks also show why the question should remain exactly in the linear-module setting and why outer automorphisms are the only nontrivial case.
